name: Rafael Gilt
preparty_markdown:
Rafael is responsible for keeping centuries-old objects from losing arguments with humidity, fingerprints,

gravity, and other people. Patient with objects and less patient with humans, he has the calm authority of

someone who has seen a priceless painting survive a flood and a donor nearly destroy one with hand lotion.

He knows what was repaired, altered, cleaned, and quietly worried over before tonight.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Dry, meticulous, tactile, slightly territorial. You care more about what is physically true than what is socially convenient.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Works closely with Celeste Frame and Calvin Case.

• Often spars intellectually with Marcus Pryce over what conservation can and cannot prove.

• Beatrice Plinth trusts Rafael's judgment more than most committees.

COSTUME

Dark suit or smart workwear made gala-appropriate; rolled sleeves under jacket, conservator gloves tucked into a pocket,

loupe or small brush as a prop.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“Nothing is 'untouched.' That is what condition reports are for.”

“Please stop breathing directly on the seventeenth century.”

about him.

altered. He threatened to replace you with a private conservator if you refused.

What you are hiding

You changed the date on a minor treatment record last month to spare the museum an embarrassing insurance dispute. No

object was harmed, but the falsification could end your career.

Do not volunteer this immediately. In Act II, protect it unless interrogation forces your hand; in Act III, reveal it if you need to defend yourself.

Your objectives

• Find out whether Calvin has noticed the altered treatment date.

• Ask Marcus what he thinks the Star Bowl's modern adhesive means.

• Keep the insurance issue separate from the murder investigation.

• Celeste quietly commissioned an outside provenance review despite pressure to stop asking questions.

• Calvin concealed a small installation crack until you could inspect it after opening night.

name: Imogen Muse
preparty_markdown:
Imogen makes expensive people uncomfortable in aesthetically impeccable ways. Her performances have

involved mirrored rooms, silent choirs, a twelve-hour dinner party, and once an empty pedestal that sold for

more than most houses. She is magnetic, playful, and perfectly capable of making a sincere point while

everyone wonders whether they are already inside the piece.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Confident, theatrical, mischievous, intelligent. Commit to bits, but never let the joke make you foolish.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Former art-school collaborator of Julian Brush; they remain close enough to annoy one another professionally.

• Lola Loom has assisted on several of Imogen's installations.

• Morgan Slate has alternated between praising and savaging Imogen in print.

COSTUME

High-fashion black tie with one strange choice: opera gloves, sculptural headpiece, monochrome outfit, dramatic makeup,

oversized flower, etc. The goal is 'gallery opening where photographers are present.'

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“If you have to ask whether it is art, the answer is already expensive.”

“No, I am not performing right now. Probably.”

Do not invent private history with Sterling Voss before game night. Your sealed party-night packet will reveal what your character actually knows

about him.
